subject: Re: Cost qualification — MedLytics inference pilot economics
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Kowalski <marta@medlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: cost qualification + open-host comparisons

Hi Marta — thanks again for today's demo. Quick recap and a few clarity asks so we can send an apples-to-apples cost sketch for the pilot.

What we took away from the call:
- Pilot scope: 3-month pilot ingesting ~250k user interactions/month (mix of short prompts + 200-token generated responses).
- Traffic mix: ~60% generation (prompt+response), ~40% embeddings/rerank calls for search.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile <350ms for short gen flows.
- Compliance: data residency in US region; standard SOC2 docs acceptable.

A few quick asks so we can benchmark $/1M token rates vs OpenAI/Anthropic and open-hosts: (if you can confirm the items below by EOD Thursday we will produce a tight target-grid)
1) Average prompt length and average generated response length (tokens) — do you expect 120 tokens end-to-end, or closer to 200?
2) Peak concurrency (QPS) expected during pilot windows?
3) Any requirement for long KV cache reuse (multi-turn chats saved per user)?
4) Target budget range for the pilot (monthly) — can you share a high/low range so we align recommendations?

Prelim note (based on what you shared): assuming 250k interactions/month, 60/40 split, and avg 160 tokens per generation exchange, that maps to roughly 24M generation tokens + 10M embedding tokens/month — ~34M total. If MedLytics wants a target per-1M-rate, we can show options: hosted Redwood standard, Redwood-dedicated (committed capacity), and an open-host parity view vs OpenAI/Anthropic public rates.

I'll attach a simple grid with a few candidate $/1M targets and the expected monthly bill across model families. Also looping Laura to keep procurement questions covered.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marta Kowalski <marta@medlytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: D. Stevens <d.stevens@medlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: cost qualification + open-host comparisons

Ben — appreciate the recap and the clear asks. Quick answers below:

1) Token lengths: median prompt ~80 tokens, median model response ~120 tokens. For planning please use 200 tokens/gen to be conservative for some analytics narratives.
2) Peak concurrency: expected peak ~18 QPS during batch report runs, but typical steady state ~2–4 QPS.
3) KV cache: we will use short-lived multi-turn sessions (per user), cache reuse expected ~10–20% hit rate.
4) Pilot budget: we have an internal pilot allocation of $8k–$12k/month; if price delta vs host parity is convincing we can expand.

Also: procurement asked us to see a simple $/1M token comparison vs OpenAI and Anthropic (public list rates) and one line comparing a committed dedicated scenario (3-month reserved) with a discounted per-1M rate. Can you include a column that separates generation vs embedding token unit rates?

Marta
VP Product, MedLytics

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Kowalski <marta@medlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: cost qualification + open-host comparisons

Marta — perfect, this is exactly what we need. Attached is a short grid (Redwood-1M-pricing-grid.pdf) and our volume assumptions (MedLytics-volume-assumptions.xlsx) with the math so you can eyeball it. A couple of notes on the benchmarking columns so the procurement folks have context:

- OpenAI / Anthropic public list: we used their published rates for text-generation and embeddings as the baseline; those are single-request hosted prices and don't include committed discounts.
- Redwood Hosted (no commit): per-1M rates slightly below list for long-form gen when we assume batching + KV caching benefits; shown in column "Hosted (est)".
- Redwood Dedicated (3-month commit): unit economics assume reserved capacity with a 20–35% discount depending on model family and quantization options; shown in column "Dedicated (3mo)".
- Open-host parity: for a fair comparison we included a column that shows what a third-party host typically bills (higher infra margins + less aggressive batching), which tends to push $/1M up by ~15–25% at low volumes.

Given your $8k–$12k pilot budget, we ran two priced scenarios in the grid: conservative (200 tok/gen) and optimistic (140 tok/gen effective). For the conservative case (200 tok/gen) your expected monthly bill at Redwood Hosted (no commit) is roughly $9.6k at $28/1M gen tokens + $12/1M embeddings (numbers illustrative — see attached). At Dedicated (3mo commit) that drops to ~$6.8k/month with a blended $/1M generation rate nearer $20.

Action items I'm proposing:
- Ben: finalize the three-row grid (done, attached) and a short 1-page note explaining assumptions (tokens, cache hit, batch efficiency).
- Marta: confirm whether procurement wants a formal quote or a draft PO for a 3-month committed trial.
- Laura/Rishi: please flag any compliance/pricing constraints for a small committed pilot (Laura: billing/legal; Rishi: infra sizing/latency SLO).

I'll follow up once procurement confirms their ask.

Thanks — Ben

Attachments: Redwood-1M-pricing-grid.pdf, MedLytics-volume-assumptions.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marta Kowalski <marta@medlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: cost qualification + open-host comparisons

Looping in procurement/legal notes — quick clarifications from our side to keep things smooth:

- If MedLytics wants a 3-month committed instance, we can produce a draft SOW and quote; typical lead time for Dedicated provisioning is ~10 business days once the PO is signed.
- Billing: we can structure the pilot as a monthly billed committed contract with a usage true-up; any overage during the pilot would be billed at the committed marginal rate.
- Compliance: SOC2 and data-residency controls are in place for US region deployments; if you need a custom data retention policy let us know, that can add a 1–2 week review.

From a pricing perspective, Rishi — can you confirm the blended $/1M generation token rate we used for the Dedicated 3mo example (we modeled $20/1M gen as the mid-case)?

Thanks — Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Head of GTM Finance, Redwood Inference
